recipes.name: Sweet Potatoes with Sausage and Peppers
ingredients_raw: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, 12 to 15 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Crumble sausage into skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until browned and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Remove sausage with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon oil from the skillet. Heat oil over medium heat and add bell peppers, onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 7 minutes.
Add to the skillet the potatoes, sausage, salsa and cumin. Stir and cook about 5 minutes to heat through and blend flavors. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potatoes with Sausage and Peppers
raw_recipe.description: Sweet potatoes, Italian sausage, and red bell peppers make spicy, savory and easy main dish. All you need is a green salad for a quick meal.

review.reviewBody: This was really surprisingly tasty! I used plain ol' bulk sausage (Jimmy Dean), browned it and then just added the veggies at that point rather than removing the sausage or adding additional oil. I 1/2" diced both the sweet potatoes and two LARGE red bell peppers, and boiled the potatoes 10 minutes -- anything more would have been mush. It makes a lot more than 4 servings in my opinion. Pita bread worked well with it, and I could see leftovers rolled in whole wheat tortillas as well. I might try a veggie sausage next time as this is so close to being a very healthy vegetarian recipe.

I made this recipe with boiling the potatoes and it was ok but I didn't like the consistency. The next time I made it I roasted the potatoes (tossed with 3/4 tsp salt, 1 TBS olive oil and 1TBS brown sugar and baked at 425 for 30 min, flipping every 10 minutes.) The taste and 
consistency was much improved!

Very good! I saute the onions and sausage, then add the sweet potatoes. When the sweet potatoes are tender, I add the peppers and salsa. Truly one-pan! Today I used chili-seasoned tomato sauce in place of the salsa, and added a few black beans. A versatile, forgiving, tasty, pantry-friendly, and healthy recipe. (I use turkey Italian sausage.) Who could ask for more?!

I made this for my very picky, veggie hating husband, a teenager and my 2 year old son (and myself who has a gluten allergy). A tough crowd to cook for. Everyone cleared their plates! I never reviewed a recipe before but this was so well received, easy and convenient that I just had to. I did make a few changes: I roasted the sweet potatoes and cooked up a pound of bulk italian sausage, left the juices and added frozen pepper and onion mix just before the sausage was fully cooked. Once cooked, I removed the juices to mix in a small amount of cornstarch and added the mixture back in along with the roasted potatoes and salsa. I didn't add any extra salt since the potatoes were salty enough. I served over black rice cooked in broth, making sure to add some he thickened juices. Yum!

New favorite! I found this recipe while searching for something to use the only ingredients I had on hand. I diced the sweet potato fairly fine and just cooked it in the pan with the sausage drippings (adding a few splashes of beef broth when it started sticking). Then I threw in a bag of frozen grilled peppers and onions (red, yellow, & green peppers) which made it super easy. Used Frontera roasted corn salsa to finish, but it tasted great even without that. Served it over rice for the family, and no rice for me for a lower carb version. Can't wait to have the leftovers with a fried egg for breakfast.

So, this was such an odd combination of flavors, but it was still good. I sliced the hot Italian sausages and cooked them separately trying to keep a portion veg friendly. I used leeks for the onions because they needed to be used. Per reviews saying the salsa was an odd mix, I used a sweet corn salsa, but added a bit of cayenne pepper to keep the heat factor. Added the sausage to half, topped all with chopped cilantro and white onion....then had shredded cheddar cheese and sour cream on the side, which was a good addition. Contrary to Mom's starch teaching, I served it over rice...per reviews...and it was a hit! Afterwards I remember I wanted to add black beans, but I'll save that for next time! Thank you for a cool, unique dinner!

First time I made exact, 2nd time because we realy liked it 
We thick sliced to the potatoes, added onions and red peppers in a foil pack with a couple tablespoons of brown sugar and oozed them on the grill until the potatoes were just tender about 10 in, as we love foil pack grilled sweet potato this way we thought why not and added the peppers and onions as we suspected the smokiness from grilling added to this dish DELIOUS

I was surprised by how much I liked this dish. Would not have thought to combine sweet potatoes + salsa + sausage. I used frozen sliced bell peppers/onion mix so there was very little prep work required. I will probably roast the potatoes next time for better flavor. I slightly overcooked them when boiling the first time and they fell apart in the final dish. This was even better leftover the next day. Will definitely make this one again!

Followed one person's suggestion to roast my sweet potatoes instead of boiling, and I think that made all of the difference. Also chose roasted red pepper chicken sausage and Mrs. Renfro's roasted salsa. The combination, along with a little shredded cheese on top was delicious. Definitely going to make again!

Baked the sweet potatoes.. took advice from a few of the comments. Easier to peel skin off after baked also.
Used Mild Salsa
Used alot more garlic ( when u tell an italian to use 2 cloves, we use 10.. or whole bulb! Ha!)
A beautiful fall dish.
High protein, low fat! 
Didn't use salt.. the salsa and italian sausage had enough.. 
This will be my lunch all week..
Thank u!

Love this!! I used chicken sausage w tomato & basil (no pork eaters in my house), medium organic salsa, yellow & red peppers, & left out the salt & pepper at the end. I'm always looking for different ways to cook sweet potatoes, and this recipe is awesome!! Definitely a keeper, & possibly perfect for potlucks! Thanks for posting!

Quick, easy, great week night dinner. Love that it includes peppers and sweet potatoes. I have family that can’t eat meat from hoof animals so they could use chicken sausage or turkey sausage in this and they would love it. I have other family that loves spice so they could put Cholula sauce in this and spice it up.. I love it just the way it is!
Great flavor and easy to make too!!!

After reading all the reviews, I decided to make this. First thing I did was cut the potatoes into bite-size pieces, coated with olive oil and roasted on 425 for 20 minutes. When I removed them, I sprinkled a little brown sugar on them. I cut my Italian sausages into bite-size pieces as well and fried them. I set them aside. I sautéed the onion, garlic, red and orange peppers. Then added the sausage and potatoes back into the pan with 1/2 can of black beans and warmed salsa. I added some ginger powder, salt and pepper, cumin, and Sazon seasoning. It turned out delicious! I served with rice.

I have made this many times and it’s delicious I will usually have enough left over for 2 or 3 more meals tastes better the next day. I have added mushroom and other left overs in my fridge before. I use 1lb bulk sausage as I don’t want to have unused meat and 16oz jar of medium salsa. Recommend this dish very easy.
Made this tonight, turned out great. Great flavours. Only issue was the so called mild sausages were a bit too hot for my wife. Next time I'll use honey garlic sausages
Pretty tasty! I roasted the sweet potatoes, but otherwise followed the recipe as is. Next time I will use more sausage and less onion.
I liked this but I thought I would like it even more. I think maybe it’s because salsa tastes a little weird with sweet potatoes. I served it over brown rice.
